payload.feature:
LANDING PR #381: deliver secret bindings to every harness (#370), and refuse any bridge transport outside the sealed audience (#371).

This branch (fix-370-371-secrets-audience, three signed commits off origin/main ba52724e) was written by hand in an interactive session. This run lands it under decision 0051: classify, verify, judge, and ship it so the contribution gate can vouch for the pull request. It is NOT a new implementation.

If verify and review are clean, nothing is edited. If a finding returns the branch to implement, fix exactly that finding and nothing beside it, add the test that proves it, show the test binds by a compiling mutation, and commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it (the hand-written head 6834b52a already measured lines 32660/32660, branches 5542/5542, functions 3187/3187).

What the reviewers should judge, from the two commits and the pull request body:
- #371: ProducerTransport::origin() and Bridge::sync_once refusing a mismatched origin before register, with one audience_matches shared by the HTTP transport; the typed BridgeError::AudienceMismatch keeps the old text; effort and reasoning_output_tokens deliberately withheld from the producer vocabulary, pinned by a test.
- #370: bind_environment as the one injector for every spawn (exec, claude, lanetally, codex, dsh), holding the sole production expose_for_spawn call (machine_proof pins exactly one); drain_stderr returning raw bytes masked by masked_text before any string exists; secret::mask_json masking decoded strings in every checkpoint, the session record and a provider refusal; the corrected docs/guides/secrets.md. Decisions 0012 (layers 3-5), 0021 ruling 4 and 0036 ruling 4 are the authority: bindings are grantable per route by egress class, so the fix delivers rather than refuses.
- Known residual, already filed as #380 and out of scope here: a secret a model echoes survives in the harness's own session file and the transcript read surfaces render it unmasked.

SECOND LANDING. The first landing run, landing-pr-381-deliver-secret-bi-f9e46580, held 3082a61e at review (REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD) with two HIGH findings: (1) the result file was masked on raw bytes before parsing, so a JSON-escaped bound value decoded back to plaintext; (2) checkpoint fields were clamped, and a refusal collapsed to one line, before masking, so a long value leaked its prefix and a value with a tab or double space no longer matched. It also noted (3) LOW: mask_json leaves a numeric value echoed as a bare JSON number; (4) INFO: ProducerTransport::origin() is a breaking trait change for out-of-tree implementors, owned by the release bump.
Commit 6834b52a answers them: every harness event (claude stream, codex stream, dsh stream-json, dsh transcript tail) is masked the moment it is parsed, before any fold, clamp or rewrite; the result file is parsed first and masked second; mask_json masks object keys; the guide records the numeric exclusion (3). Each fix has a test bound by a removal control. Judge whether the findings are closed, and whether any surface a bound value can reach the journal through is still masked after a clamp or decode.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],

    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of 8d210dd9 (#371) and 3082a61e + 6834b52a (#370) on fix-370-371-secrets-audience, read against origin/main ba52724e. I tried to break the masking pipeline rather than confirm it. No high/critical finding; security-hold is NOT warranted. Details:

FINDING 1 (prior HIGH) CLOSED. The result file is now parsed with serde_json::from_str and then secret::mask_json'd (adapters.rs:6108-6115); the unparseable branch masks the error string. I verified the ordering by reading the hunk and by running the bound test a_result_file_quoting_an_escaped_bound_value_is_journaled_masked, which uses API_TOKEN = zq"7w\k-leak-value and passes; reordering to the old raw-bytes-first pass would decode the escape back to plaintext and fail it. The only string that escapes masking is a bare JSON number, which is the documented exclusion (see residual below).

FINDING 2 (prior HIGH) CLOSED. Each of the four harness event sources is masked the moment it is parsed, before any fold/clamp/rewrite: claude/lanetally stream (adapters.rs:2423), codex stream (3083), dsh stream-json (4229), dsh transcript tail (2296). The result-file, session_meta values and refusal prose are masked at the run_seat choke points (5799, 5907-5910). The four removal-control tests (long target clamp, tab+double-space refusal, codex error event, dsh tool/call) pass; on the un-fixed ordering each would journal a prefix or a rewritten form that no whole-needle mask can match. All new tests and the expose_for_spawn single-call-site machine proof pass locally.

#371 CLEAN. audience_matches is the single rule; Bridge::sync_once applies it to any ProducerTransport::origin() after dispatch.verify and before transport.register (lib.rs:607), the mock test proves zero registrations and zero submitted events for empty/suffix-spoof/path-appended/wrong-host origins, and HttpTransport::new already trims base_url so the shared rule preserves old behavior. AudienceMismatch display text is byte-identical to the old Transport(...) rendering and is pinned; no other in-tree code matched the old string.

RESIDUAL (LOW, security): a wholly numeric bound value echoed as a bare JSON number is still not masked by mask_json (secret.rs:627-646 leaves Value::Number untouched). Concrete inputs: bind TOKEN=12345678, run a claude seat whose shim emits {"type":"assistant",...,"usage":{"input_tokens":12345678}}; positive_count reads the number and the session-finished checkpoint journals input_tokens:12345678 into the append-only journal. The same holds for a numeric result-file field. This was finding (3) of the first landing; commit 6834 documents it in docs/guides/secrets.md but the leak remains. I kept the low severity because it needs a digits-only secret, which the guide now explicitly tells operators not to bind.

INFO, not security: (a) ProducerTransport::origin() is a new required trait method, a semver break for out-of-tree implementors, owned by the release bump (finding 4, unchanged); (b) mask_json masking object keys can collapse two keys that mask to the same string (e.g. bind API_TOKEN=key, result file {"key":1,"[secret:API_TOKEN]":2}), serde_json::Map::insert silently drops one field - a low data-loss edge, not a leak and not key-spoofing, since the replacement text is always [secret:NAME]; (c) JSON-escaped secrets in raw child stderr are not caught by masked_text, but stderr is never parsed/decoded by the driver (the bytes are journaled still escaped) and decision 0012 'What this does not promise' explicitly disclaims a child transforming a value into an unlisted shape, so I did not raise it; the guide's stderr wording ('on raw bytes') is accurate. The known #380 model-echo/session-file residual is out of scope per the commission.
members.correctness: Judged the three signed commits (8d210dd9 #371, 3082a61e #370, 6834b52a second-landing answers) against origin/main ba52724e, the framing, decisions 0012/0021 r4/0036 r4/0051 and the guide. Both HIGH findings from the first landing are closed. (1) Result file: adapters.rs now parses first (from_utf8_lossy -> serde_json::from_str) and masks the parsed value with secret::mask_json; the unparseable branch masks its serde error string; a_result_file_quoting_an_escaped_bound_value_is_journaled_masked drives the production run_seat path with a value containing a quote and a backslash (serde escapes them on the wire) and pins notes == 'used [secret:API_TOKEN]' with no plaintext in any message — removing the mask call would fail it. (2) Clamp/collapse: every harness event is masked at parse before any fold — claude/lanetally stream, codex stream, dsh stream-json and the dsh transcript tail (four call sites, all passing bindings) — so the 80-char tool/target clamps and bounded_wire_line's whitespace collapse read masked text; four per-arm tests bind this (claude long target pins target == '/work/[secret:API_TOKEN]' with no prefix; claude refusal with tab and double space; codex error event with a long value; dsh transcript tool call with a long value). The belt-and-braces re-masks in run_seat (session_meta via mask_json, refusal via masked_text) are idempotent and harmless. Sweep for surfaces a bound value can still reach the journal through after a clamp or decode: none found — checkpoints, session record, refusal, transcript locator ids and dsh launch rows all derive from masked events or raw-byte-masked captures (drain_stderr at all four spawns, exec stdout/state, dsh stderr masked before redact_dsh_reasoning, which only drops lines); the codex thread-file echo extracts bounded model/effort fields only; dsh resume-boundary evidence reads structural fields only; no decode/unescape step resurrects plaintext. Finding (3) LOW numeric exclusion is closed as a deliberate documented exclusion: mask_json masks strings and object keys, leaves numbers (mask_json_masks_object_keys_and_leaves_numbers_as_numbers pins it) and the guide now says 'do not bind a secret that is only digits' — masking bare numbers would corrupt the seat record's u64 usage counts, and the raw-byte surfaces still catch digits; residual drops to info. Finding (4) INFO stands: ProducerTransport::origin() has exactly two in-tree impls (HttpTransport, test mock), both updated; the breaking change for out-of-tree implementors is owned by the release version bump. My own info-grade observations: mask_json's key remap can collapse two distinct keys into one masked key (contrived, seat-authored result file only), and HttpTransport's origin comparison now trims trailing slashes on both sides — a deliberate, tested admit-direction normalization of a same-origin spelling, more correct origin semantics. #371 re-verified: Bridge::sync_once applies audience_matches after the run-id check and before transport.register; four hostile origins (wrong port, suffix-spoof, path-appended, empty) are refused with zero registrations and zero events, trailing-slash admit pinned both ways, BridgeError::AudienceMismatch display byte-pinned to the old Transport rendering; safe_checkpoint withholds effort/reasoning_output_tokens and a test pins the exclusion. bind_environment remains the sole injector for all five harness kinds and holds the only production expose_for_spawn call (machine_proof grep test passes). Frozen bytes untouched — the diff is two crates plus docs/guides/secrets.md, which matches the code exactly. Gates: cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked green (exit 0, no failures), cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean. Three Good GPG signatures; working tree clean; this seat edited nothing. No security finding from this seat; the known #380 session-file residual stays out of scope as filed.

result.notes:
Review chief, second landing of PR #381 (8d210dd9, 3082a61e, 6834b52a against ba52724e). PANEL: both members reported and both ruled residual. The joined result was residual, low, security=true, spec_defect=false, so that is the floor and I did not lower it. The members are named adversarial and correctness, not security and correctness; adversarial did the security work. Neither member's text is addressed to the gate or argues for a verdict. Adversarial's line 'security-hold is NOT warranted' is its own severity call, and I checked it rather than copying it. Correctness moved finding (3) down to info in its own view. The panel's max is still LOW security, and I kept that.

MY OWN READ (the full diff, and the traced paths): prior HIGH (1) is CLOSED. The result file is parsed first and masked second (adapters.rs:6108-6115), and the unparseable branch masks the serde error text. Prior HIGH (2) is CLOSED. The claude/lanetally stream (2423), codex stream (3083), dsh stream-json (4229) and dsh transcript tail (2296) each mask the decoded event with mask_json before any fold, clamp or one-line rewrite. The commission asked whether any journal surface still masks after a clamp or decode. I found none. I traced: checkpoints, which are masked at parse and masked again at the run_seat choke point; session_meta, masked at 5908, and served_model, which model_token refuses rather than truncates; the stderr tail, masked on raw bytes at all four spawns and sliced afterwards; the refusal reason, masked at parse and bounded afterwards; the codex thread echo, whose model/effort grammar refuses rather than truncates and which the choke point re-masks; invoke Err strings, which are fixed text; and the dsh promotion summary, which is a ref name plus oids. Cross-event concatenation that could rebuild a split needle: none found. #371 is clean. audience_matches is the one rule. sync_once applies it after dispatch.verify (safe_audience) and before register. HttpTransport behaviour is unchanged, and AudienceMismatch prints the same text as before. bind_environment covers all four Command spawns, and machine_proof pins exactly one expose_for_spawn call. Frozen bytes are untouched. I ran these crate-scoped: brokkr-protocol, 42 masking/binding/refusal/clamp tests; brokkr-bridge, 16/16; and the machine_proof expose_for_spawn test. All green. I edited nothing.

SURVIVING FINDINGS, one list:
1. LOW, security (adversarial; correctness concurs, calling it info). mask_json leaves a JSON number untouched (secret.rs, the mask_json match arm `_ => {}`), so a secret made only of digits and echoed as a bare number is journaled in plaintext, for example as a numeric field in the result file. This is a documented exclusion in docs/guides/secrets.md, and the fix is deferred. It is kept at LOW rather than closed.
2. INFO (adversarial + correctness). mask_json can map two keys to the same masked key, and Map::insert then silently drops one. That loses data. It does not leak anything and cannot forge anything.
3. INFO (adversarial + correctness, first landing's finding 4). ProducerTransport::origin() is a new required trait method, which breaks out-of-tree implementors. The release bump owns that.
4. INFO (correctness). Both sides of the origin comparison now trim trailing slashes. This admits two spellings of the same origin, and a test pins it.
5. INFO (adversarial). JSON-escaped secrets in raw child stderr are not masked. Decision 0012 disclaims transformed values.
6. INFO (chief). Masking now runs before the fold. A bound value of 4 bytes or more that equals a protocol word or key (type, result, error, usage) would rewrite control fields, so the fold could miss a result, refusal or usage event, and a matching key in the result file would park. The effect is lost telemetry or a fail-closed park, never a leak.
7. INFO (chief). A stale comment at adapters.rs:6096-6099 still says 'Raw bytes first, string conversion second', directly above 'Parsed FIRST and masked second'. The test name mask_json_masks_every_decoded_string_and_leaves_keys_and_scalars says keys are left, but keys are now masked. mask_bytes' BUFFERED-ONLY INVARIANT comment still says every surface is a wait_with_output buffer. Per-line stream masking is correct, because each event is one complete line, but the comment is out of date.
Out of scope as filed: #380 (a model's echo survives in the session file and in the transcript read surfaces).
Nothing above LOW, so this does not return to implement.
